Bible home File tree Sequence Inspectors Missing log Old QC packet

Inspectors — pass / fail / save

First pass = 2-story light wood (SFR / ADU). Not apartments. Not 3-story. Not steel. 30 Aug 2026.

This is book hold points from filed Methods. Not a stamp. Not an AHJ fail list. AHJ fail lists stay a Gap until a book names them.

Logan ice barrier is on the city sheet (P09). Fontana does not get a Utah snow pack. Fontana Title 24 is P13. P01 is site prep, not foundation. P04 drainage is not the foundation drain. No skip-inspection.

Each method below is LOOKS AT (book hold points), DO NOT CHEAP (only if the book already calls it a hold, a permit gate, or a layering requirement), and SMART SAVE (from the book’s time/money note — if missing: “Gap — book did not name a save”). Late-swap risk is under SMART SAVE when the book named it. P03 habit is batter boards (FM 5-426 Ch 4; m-P03-batter-boards filed). ORNL / HUD / AF&PA have no batter-board procedure — do not stretch P01 stakes into this Method. CMHC offsets are Canadian — confirm AHJ.

P00 — Intake / feasibility

On a 2-story stick house this is desk work before dirt. Method filed: m-P00-drawings-before-permit (habit, high). Delivery method is a Gap. Crew count is a Gap. CMHC is Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.

m-P00-drawings-before-permit — drawings / contract / permit (habit)

Permit gate: this phase IS the gate. Foundation type and radon stub on the drawings. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. Not a stamp. Not legal advice.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Zoning for the intended use before planning (CMHC Ch2). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
  • Drawings to scale for a plans examiner (CMHC Ch2).
  • Complete plans and specifications; bid package; contract that references blueprints and specs; excavation allowance; building permits acquired (ORNL PLANS, CONTRACTS, AND BUILDING PERMITS).
  • Drawings and specs before the permit (hold + permit gate).
  • Contract that references the blueprints and specs, with an excavation allowance (ORNL).
  • Foundation type and radon stub on the drawings now.

CMHC: pre-construction duration is variable by site and house. No dollars. Do not invent days.

Late swap: foundation type or radon/termite path after permit is a type change. Catch on the drawings.

Mess-ups: Gap until the book names them. Delivery-method alts: Gap (gap-P00-delivery-method-alts). Do not copy CMHC’s Canadian permit menu as IRC.

P01 — Site prep

On a 2-story stick house this is locate, survey, strip, test hole — not the foundation. Methods filed: m-P01-site-prep (habit), m-P01-geotech-spt and m-P01-geotech-dcp (alts when R401.4 requires a report). Demo of an existing house is a Gap.

m-P01-site-prep — survey / locate / strip / test hole (habit)

P01 is site prep, not foundation. Confirm with AHJ. Not a stamp. CMHC surveyor/utility language is Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Utility locate; buried cables, pipes, sewers protected (ORNL SITEWORK; CMHC Ch6).
  • Stakes and benchmarks; lot corners from a certified surveyor (ORNL; CMHC).
  • Test hole, full depth, in the proposed foundation location; water table (ORNL).
  • Topsoil stripped and stockpiled; spoil site defined; stumps/grubbing off (ORNL; CMHC).
  • Utility locate before you dig (hold).
  • Test hole in the proposed foundation location (hold).
  • Strip organics / stumps off the foundation area.
  • Geotech report when IRC R401.4 requires it (permit gate) — see SPT/DCP alts.

HUD: tests on stronger-than-average soils can justify smaller footings — that is the report, not a field guess. CMHC: reuse stripped topsoil. No dollars.

Late swap: a soils surprise changes foundation type. Catch with the test hole / geotech before permit.

Mess-ups (sourced): cutting telephone, gas or power lines (CMHC Ch6); leaving stumps and scrap in the foundation area (ORNL). Demo of an existing house: Gap.

m-P01-geotech-spt — SPT report (alt)

HUD §4.3 / ASTM D1586. Rare on ordinary SFR. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. Not a stamp.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Report in hand when R401.4 requires it (HUD).
  • 2-in sampler, 140-lb hammer, 30-in drop; blow count per foot (HUD). Designer reads Table 4.3.
  • Do not substitute the presumptive table as a skip when R401.4 requires a report.

HUD: SPT usually not warranted for typical residential. DCP is the documented cheaper equal. No dollars.

Mess-ups: inventing a geotech on every lot; using Table 4.3 without an engineer. AHJ fail list: Gap beyond the require-vs-table fork.

m-P01-geotech-dcp — DCP report (alt)

HUD §4.3 handheld cone. Same R401.4 gate as SPT. Confirm with AHJ / engineer.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Report in hand when R401.4 requires it.
  • 17.6-lb weight, 2.26-ft drop; blows per 1-3/4 in ≈ SPT (HUD).
  • Do not treat a small uncalibrated penetrometer as a deep-strata test (HUD).

HUD names DCP as a more economical alternative with equivalent accuracy vs SPT. No dollars. Smaller pens may miss deep problems.

Mess-ups: calling an uncalibrated pen DCP. AHJ fail list: Gap.

P02 — Permits, zoning, approvals, testing

On a 2-story stick house this is the paper gate. Nothing in the ground until the paper is real. Method filed: m-P02-permit-holds (habit, high). Not legal advice. No skip-inspection. HOA / impact fees / special inspector: Gap. CMHC Fig 2 is Canadian — do not copy as IRC.

m-P02-permit-holds — permit and inspection ladder (habit)

ORNL: acquire building permits. Inspection ladder is dual-use design and field. Filed P05/P07/P08 types still belong on the drawings before permit. Confirm with AHJ. Not a stamp. No skip-inspection.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Building permit in hand before the hole (ORNL; CMHC Fig 2). Confirm AHJ.
  • After excavation, before footing concrete (ORNL first site inspection).
  • After footings, before walls; after foundation + dampproofing, before rough framing.
  • After rough framing; after rough plumbing and electrical.
  • Insulation before drywall — and before backfill when foam is outside.
  • Final. How much notice before calling (CMHC). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
  • Permit before dirt (hold + permit gate).
  • After-excavation-before-footing-pour inspection (ORNL).
  • Excavation allowance written into the contract (ORNL / P00).
  • PE when tables fail (HUD) — not a PE stamp as a default on a table house.
  • Do not skip because CMHC said some municipalities do not inspect every stage. Ask.

CMHC: schedule inspections to avoid lengthy delays. HUD: IRC path lets builder + official inspect without a PE until tables fail. No dollars.

Late swap: foundation type after permit is a type change. Working ahead of a hold is a stop-work, not a save.

Mess-ups: Gap as an AHJ fail list. Do not copy CMHC’s Canadian permit menu as IRC. HOA / impact fees / special inspector: Gap (gap-P02-hoa-impact-special-inspect).

P03 — Layout / batter boards / temp facilities

On a 2-story stick house this puts the house on the dirt. Method filed: m-P03-batter-boards (habit, high) from FM 5-426 Ch4. CMHC Ch6 is Canadian — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Temp toilet is a Gap. Same craft on a Fontana slab and a Logan basement.

m-P03-batter-boards — boards and string (habit)

FM is US technique. CMHC offsets/millimetres are Canadian. Confirm setbacks with AHJ. Not a stamp. 6-8-10 and equal diagonals are variants inside this Method.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Corner stakes first; batter boards 3 or 4 ft outside so the hole does not eat the lines (FM).
  • Boards level; tops at top of foundation (FM).
  • Square: 6-8-10 (never start under 6 ft) or equal diagonals (FM). CMHC 12-16-20 in triangulation is Canadian — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
  • Separate saw cuts or nails for building / foundation / footing / excavation lines (FM). 8d named for the string.
  • Plumb bob over corner stakes; lines level (FM).
  • Do not skip batter boards and hope corner stakes survive the bucket (FM).
  • Do not start 6-8-10 on a stick shorter than 6 ft (FM).
  • Do not copy CMHC 24–28 in excavation width or millimetre 3-4-5 as US habit.
  • Do not walk the house onto a setback (CMHC). Confirm with AHJ.

6-8-10 vs diagonals is not a product upgrade. Irregular plan: big rectangle first (FM). Kerfs let you pull string for the machine and put it back. No dollars. Toilet: Gap (gap-P03-temp-toilet).

Late swap: moving corners after the hole is a reshoot. Catch vs survey and the permit set.

Mess-ups: Gap until the book names them. Do not use FM rubble/column foundations in the same chapter as a P05 type swap.

P04 — Excavation / grading / drainage

On a 2-story stick house this is the hole. Wasatch/Logan basement-deep because 30-in frost is already filed. Fontana is a slab scrape. P04 drainage is not the foundation drain. Methods filed: m-P04-full-excavation (habit), m-P04-trench-footing (Canadian well-drained alt), m-P04-sog-strip (Fontana/South alt).

m-P04-full-excavation — basement/crawl hole (habit, Wasatch / Logan)

After excavation and before footing concrete (ORNL). Drain tile holes-down is P05 CIP/CMU, not this phase. Confirm with AHJ. Not a stamp. CMHC 24–28 in workspace is Canadian — do not copy as US habit.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Hole open; utilities/trees protected (ORNL SITEWORK).
  • Bottom not frozen (ORNL FOOTINGS; CMHC winter).
  • Overexcavated trench not filled with loose dirt; not bearing half-on-rock (ORNL).
  • Filled ground / root-removal zones compacted (AF&PA).
  • Back slope or shore a deep cut (CMHC). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Do not invent OSHA 5-ft.
  • After-excavation-before-footing-pour inspection (ORNL hold).
  • Do not fill the overexcavated trench. Do not pour on frozen ground. Do not bear half-on-rock.
  • Do not dump roof water into the P05 tile (CMHC/ORNL separate systems).
  • Do not shop drain tile into P04 — tile, holes-down, is P05 CIP/CMU only.

CMHC: reuse excavated material; set elevation to minimize rock. ORNL: do not blast a basement into shallow bedrock just to chase frost. No dollars. Compaction % not named — do not invent 95%.

Late swap: hole depth follows P05 type. Catch before permit.

Mess-ups (sourced): frozen soils; cave-ins on an unsloped deep cut; filling overexcavation; roof leaders into the foundation drain.

m-P04-trench-footing — trench to top of footings (alt, Canadian)

CMHC Ch6 well-drained shortcut. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Not a US habit.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Main excavation only to top of footings; footings trenched on undisturbed soil (CMHC).
  • Space outside the footing for the drain pipe (CMHC).
  • Same ORNL footing inspect before pour.
  • Do not skip drain-pipe space. Do not use this alt on a wet site or where a granular base under the slab is required.

Shallower main hole on a well-drained site. Confirm AHJ. No dollars.

Mess-ups: using this on a wet lot. AHJ fail list: Gap.

m-P04-sog-strip — slab strip (alt, Fontana / South)

No basement hole. HUD §4.1 slab in warmer regions. Confirm with AHJ. Not a stamp.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Debris, stumps, organics gone under the slab (CMHC Ch7).
  • Compacted granular, no soft pockets (CMHC; ORNL compact fill under slab).
  • Finish floor high enough that grade drains away. CMHC 6 in vs ORNL ≥8 in — confirm AHJ; do not pick a winner.
  • Do not leave organics under the slab.
  • Do not shop P05 drain tile onto an above-grade SOG as habit.

No basement hole on a Fontana/South SOG. No drain tile if the floor is above grade (ORNL Ch 4). No dollars.

Late swap: slab vs basement after permit is a type change.

Mess-ups: leaving organics under the slab. Compaction % Gap. AHJ fail list: Gap.

P06 — Underslab MEP / radon / termite

On a 2-story stick house this is what goes in before the slab. A basement house still has a basement slab; a Fontana house has the first-floor slab. Methods filed: m-P06-underslab-prep (habit), m-P06-radon-standpipe and m-P06-termite-soil-treat (alts where the hazard exists). Drain tile is P05. Fontana vs Utah split is a Gap. On SOG this is before the pour in the field even if the spine reads P05→P06. Do not rewrite P05 Methods.

m-P06-underslab-prep — plumbing / gravel / poly / wood out (habit)

12-in laps already a P05 class; this is the before-pour sequence. Confirm with AHJ. Not a stamp. CMHC is Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Sewer/subsurface work in; trench backfill compacted (CMHC) before the slab.
  • Gravel bed (ORNL 4-in coarse clean / HUD §4.6 2–3 in — do not pick a winner; follow AHJ).
  • 6-mil poly, 12-in laps, sealed to wall or over footing (ORNL).
  • Penetrations X-cut, tabs taped; pipe penetrations caulked (ORNL).
  • No wood left in the pour (ORNL).
  • Plumbing in first (hold).
  • 6-mil polyethylene, 12-in laps, sealed to the wall (hold + layering).
  • Wood / grade stakes out of the pour (hold).

Optional 2-in sand over the poly is ORNL optional, not a required extra Method. HUD 2–3 in vs ORNL 4 in — confirm AHJ; not a field cheap-out. No dollars.

Late swap: adding radon or termite after the slab is a retrofit. Catch on the drawings.

Mess-ups (sourced): puncturing poly on sharp gravel; leaving grade stakes in the slab. Underslab plumber how-to (pipe sizes) is CLASS, not a schedule. AHJ fail list: Gap beyond wood-in-pour / disturbed treated soil.

m-P06-radon-standpipe — capped standpipe in gravel (alt where radon is probable)

ORNL §2.2 / Figs 2-5 and 2-6. AF&PA and HUD RSDG silent on the standpipe — silence is not a veto. Contact state health. CMHC NBC methods and 200 Bq/m³ are Canadian — do not copy as EPA. Confirm with AHJ. Not a stamp. Not printed as Utah-only.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Capped 3- or 4-in PVC standpipe in the subslab gravel (ORNL). Single standpipe OK on typical house-size floor with clean coarse gravel.
  • 4-in coarse gravel + 6-mil poly still in (habit). The pipe is not a skip of poly.
  • Caulked slab penetrations and wall-slab joint (ORNL).
  • Sump cover airtight if a sump exists. No open floor drain to the gravel without a mechanical trap.
  • Capped standpipe during construction (hold).
  • Do not skip the roof-stack-during-construction path to “save” a chase (ORNL: normally less costly now than later).
  • Polyurethane at the wall-slab joint and penetrations.

ORNL: stack through the roof during construction is normally less costly than after finish. Passive (no fan) first; fan later if tests say so. No dollars printed.

Mess-ups: leaving the standpipe out to “drill later” as the habit; open sump in a radon-prone basement; copying CMHC 200 Bq/m³ as a US action level. Fontana vs Utah split: Gap (gap-P06-fontana-utah-split).

m-P06-termite-soil-treat — soil treatment before the pour (alt where termites are a hazard)

Consult local officials (ORNL). AF&PA: soil treatment is the most effective subterranean path. Shields optional, not a substitute (D8). Confirm with AHJ. Not a stamp. Not printed as Fontana-only. CMHC termite map is Canadian.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Treated soil still undisturbed (ORNL: do not disturb prior to concreting).
  • No wood stakes / spreaders / scrap in the foundation area or in the pour (ORNL; AF&PA).
  • Sill 8 in / siding 6 in above grade when those members are in (ORNL) — often a later look.
  • Soil termiticide on vulnerable sites, especially with insulated foundations (ORNL hold).
  • Wood / form stakes out of the pour.
  • Do not disturb treated soil before concreting.
  • Do not trade treatment for shields (D8).

ORNL: treatment is the most effective technique with insulated foundations; shields are not a cheaper skip. No dollars. Applicator license not named.

Late swap: treating after the slab is a different job. Catch before the pour.

Mess-ups (sourced): leaving form stakes in the pour; walking treated soil; trading treatment for a shield; leaving roots/stumps/scrap in the foundation area. Fontana vs Utah split: Gap.

P18 — Punch / inspections / CO / turnover

On a 2-story stick house this is the inspection ladder through CO. Filed as m-P18-inspections-co. Punch-list procedure is a Gap (opened Ch2 and Ch29 — Ch29 is maintenance). No skip-inspection. Not a stamp. Not the P05/P07/P08 rollup. Card at the end of this page.

m-P18-inspections-co — see also the P18 card below

CMHC Fig 2 Certificate of Occupancy is Canadian. Confirm with AHJ. Punch-list walk/form is gap-P18-punch-list. Not a stamp. No skip-inspection.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Foundations, framing, plumbing and electrical, insulation, exterior finishes actually inspected (CMHC p 12). Confirm with AHJ.
  • Contractor punch list complete (Goetsch Ch 7).
  • Architect punch + substantial completion only if an architect is on the job (Goetsch). Gap for spec SFR.
  • Completion inspection interior and exterior; Certificate of Occupancy (CMHC Fig 2). Confirm with AHJ.
  • Operating instructions and warranties in the owner’s hands; final clean-up (CMHC p 22).
  • Do not skip inspections. Do not skip CO.
  • Do not treat this page as a stamp.
  • Do not treat substantial completion as a substitute for the AHJ occupancy inspection.
  • Do not reopen P05/P07/P08 holds as punch “saves.”

Goetsch: contractor punch before the architect walk so you are not walking twice — no dollars named. CMHC: schedule notice so the job does not sit. Gap — book did not name a save. No skip-inspection save.

Mess-ups: Gap until the book names them.

P05 — Foundation

On a 2-story stick house this is the thing the walls sit on. Utah basement vs Fontana slab is already filed. Crew count is a Gap.

Do-not-cheap we already know (filed SOP):

  • 1/2-in bolts
  • Drain tile holes-down (CIP/CMU only, not PWF, not Fontana valley slab as habit)
  • Poly laps
  • Waterproof before backfill

m-P05-basement-cip-cmu — CIP / CMU basement (habit, Wasatch / Logan)

Permit gate: should be on drawings before permit. Foundation type on drawings. Engineer when IRC tables fail or unreinforced wall limits exceeded. Not a stamp.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Footing inspection before pour; no frozen subgrade (ORNL).
  • Wall forms, steel, and bolt layout before pour; no extra water (ORNL / HUD §4.2).
  • Waterproofing before backfill; protection board on exterior foam to 6 in below grade (ORNL note 1).
  • Soil treatment before slab; form wood out of the pour (ORNL).
  • Floor framing in before significant backfill of basement walls (HUD §4.5).
  • ORNL Fig 1-4 last step: establish QC inspection procedures; Ch 2 checklists dual-use design and field. AF&PA: inspector enforces the illustrated procedures. HUD: IRC so builder + official can inspect without a PE; PE when tables fail.
  • Radon standpipe in subslab gravel, cap, preferably stack through roof during construction (ORNL §2.2 only — not in AF&PA or HUD RSDG). Med confidence; regional.
  • Fastener named: sill anchor bolts 1/2 in, ~6 ft o.c., ≤1 ft from corners (ORNL notes 13/31; AF&PA Sills). Embed is D2 — follow AHJ.
  • 1/2-in sill bolts (hold / fastener / SOP).
  • Waterproof before backfill (hold + layering).
  • Drain tile: 4-in perf, holes down, 1 in in 20 ft, gravel envelope, filter fabric (layering, ORNL note 8). CIP/CMU only. Not PWF.
  • 6-mil poly, 12-in laps (layering).
  • Waterproof on the wall, insulation outboard of it, down to the footing drain (layering, ORNL note 6).
  • Protection board on exterior foam to 6 in below grade (layering / hold).
  • Basement slab isolation joint at wall; slab floats — not on a wall ledge (layering).
  • Permit gate: foundation type on drawings before permit.

CIP vs CMU is a yard/skill choice, not a physics winner (ORNL §1.3). Drain tile is basement detailing, not a type swap. No dollars in sources.

Late swap: swapping basement vs slab/crawl after permit is a type change: excavation depth, waterproofing, drain tile, floor package, and stairs all move. Catch before permit.

Mess-ups: Gap until the book names them.

m-P05-slab — slab-on-grade (habit, Fontana / South)

Permit gate: should be on drawings before permit. Foundation type (slab vs basement vs crawl) and any FPSF detail on drawings. Engineer when expansive / tables fail.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Soil treatment before slab; form wood out of the pour (ORNL).
  • Vapor retarder in place; 6-mil laps (HUD §4.6; ORNL).
  • Footing / thickened-edge layout before pour; no frozen subgrade if any frost-depth stem is used.
  • FPSF foam/termite path inspection in high-termite regions if FPSF is used (HUD §4.8).
  • No joist package on SOG South (c-P07-no-joists-on-sog).
  • Fastener named: sill anchor bolts 1/2 in, ~6 ft o.c., ≤1 ft from corners (same family as CIP/CMU). Embed D2 — follow AHJ.
  • 1/2-in sill bolts (fastener / SOP).
  • 6-mil poly, 12-in laps (hold + layering). HUD §4.6: 2–3 in sand/gravel + 6-mil.
  • Soil treatment before slab; form wood out of the pour (hold).
  • No subdrain / waterproofing if floor is above grade (layering, ORNL Ch 4). Not Fontana valley slab drain tile as habit.
  • No joist package on SOG South (hold).
  • Elevate slab ≥8 in above grade (layering, ORNL Ch 4).
  • Permit gate: slab vs basement vs crawl on drawings before permit.

No joist package on Fontana/South SOG. No drain tile/waterproof if the floor is above grade. Edge insulation/thermal break is a detailing add, not a new foundation type. No dollars in sources.

Late swap: slab vs basement after permit is a type change: no joists, no basement stairs, different excavation. Catch before permit.

Mess-ups: Gap until the book names them.

m-P05-crawl — crawl-space wall or piers

Permit gate: should be on drawings before permit. Crawl vs basement after permit changes excavation, drainage, vents, and first-floor height.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Footing inspection before pour; no frozen subgrade (ORNL).
  • Soil treatment before covering the crawl floor / before any slab pour in the crawl.
  • Clearances 12 in girder / 18 in joist (AF&PA); post clearance D7.
  • Vent vs unvented per adopted IRC/energy code, not a winner from this set (D1).
  • If below-grade wall is waterproofed, that coating before backfill (ORNL).
  • Fastener named: sill anchor bolts 1/2 in, ~6 ft o.c., ≤1 ft from corners. Embed D2 — follow AHJ.
  • 1/2-in sill bolts (fastener / SOP).
  • Ground cover: 6-mil poly over all exposed soil, 12-in laps, edges to wall (layering).
  • Wood-to-earth clearance: 12 in earth-to-girder, 18 in earth-to-joist (layering).
  • Drain tile only if crawl floor is below grade on tight soil — 4-in perf, holes down, 1 in in 20 ft (layering). NOT PWF.
  • Waterproof-before-backfill still applies to a below-grade crawl face (hold).
  • Permit gate: type on drawings before permit.

Shallower hole than basement. Drain tile only if the crawl floor is below grade on tight soil. Do not sell a vent kit as if D1 were settled. No dollars in sources.

Late swap: crawl vs basement after permit changes excavation, drainage, vents, and first-floor height. Catch before permit.

Mess-ups: Gap until the book names them.

m-P05-pwf — permanent wood foundation (alt, not the regional default)

Permit gate: should be on drawings before permit. PWF / treated-wall system on drawings (HUD Fig 4.9 / Table 4.8).

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Treated material and gravel-bed thickness before walls (AF&PA; ORNL note 27).
  • No drain tile to look for — inspect gravel path to sump instead (D9).
  • 6-mil on basement walls and under floor.
  • PWF / treated-wall system on drawings before permit (HUD Fig 4.9 / Table 4.8).
  • Gravel bed ≥4 in (AF&PA) / ≥6 in thick and 6 in past the plate (layering, ORNL note 27).
  • 6-mil on basement walls and under floor (hold + layering).
  • No conventional drain tile — gravel to sump (layering D9). Do not shop drain tile onto PWF.
  • Batt in cavities; 2-in air gap above the bottom plate (layering, ORNL note 35).
  • Permit gate: PWF on drawings before permit.
  • Fastener size+oc is not in the extract (fastener_schedule is empty). Do not invent 8d/10d/16d.

Winter/prefab is the reason to pick it (AF&PA). Gravel-to-sump instead of a pour and drain tile — not a cheaper tile skip (D9). No dollars in sources.

Late swap: PWF vs CIP/CMU after permit changes excavation, drainage (no tile), treated package, and inspection path. Catch before permit.

Mess-ups: Gap until the book names them.

m-P05-waterproof — below-grade coating (step, not a foundation type)

Permit gate: should be on drawings before permit. Finished-basement waterproof vs dampproof should show on drawings. Not a P08 item.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Form-tie holes plugged / CMU parged before coating (ORNL).
  • Waterproofing (or dampproofing as chosen) in place before backfill (ORNL note 1).
  • Protection board on exterior foam to 6 in below grade (ORNL note 1).
  • Drain tile laid holes-down, gravel, fabric, outfall or sump, not tied to roof leaders (ORNL note 8) — CIP/CMU only.
  • Waterproof before backfill (hold + SOP). You cannot coat after the dirt is in without digging the walls back out.
  • CMU: parge, then dampproof/asphalt. CIP: plug form-tie holes before waterproofing (layering).
  • Waterproof on the wall, insulation outboard of it, down to the footing drain (layering).
  • Protection board on exterior foam to 6 in below grade (hold + layering).
  • Drain tile: 4-in perf, holes down, 1 in in 20 ft (layering). NOT PWF (D9).
  • Permit gate: finished-basement waterproof vs dampproof on drawings.
  • No fastener size+oc in this coating sequence. Do not invent.

Waterproof vs dampproof is a basement detailing choice before backfill; you cannot swap after the dirt is in. Drain tile is not a PWF skip. No dollars in sources.

Late swap: you cannot swap dampproof for waterproof after backfill without digging the walls back out.

Mess-ups: Gap until the book names them.

P07 — Floor structure

On a 2-story Utah house the first floor is wood on the basement. On a Fontana slab the slab is the first floor — no joist truck on a valley slab. Stairs opening in the floor is a hold for the P08 stair well, not a new floor type.

Do-not-cheap we already know (filed SOP):

  • 1-3/4 in bearing
  • AFG-01 glue
  • Subfloor 6/12
  • Brace before walk
  • No joist truck on Fontana slab

m-P07-i-joist — I-joist platform floor (volume habit)

Permit gate: should be on drawings before permit. I-joist layout / ESR on drawings. Engineer when tables fail (HUD). Good first offer: I-joist vs sawn is a permit-gate framing choice.

LOOKS ATDO NOT CHEAPSMART SAVE
  • Grade-marked / ESR product on site (AF&PA grade-mark family; HUD §1.3 shop drawings/ESR).
  • Brace before walk; no stack on unsheathed joists (PJI p 3).
  • No flange cuts; holes only as tabled; stiffeners when required (PJI Notes 1–13).
  • Sheathing glue on if using catalog spans (PJI).

P08 — Walls / shear / stairs

On a 2-story stick house the walls go up on the platform (or on the Fontana slab). Habit is 2x4 at 16 in. Stairs are cut-stringer after the well is in. A 2-story house has a flight either way. Kick plate on basement concrete is the Utah basement bottom, not a hanger.

Do-not-cheap we already know (filed SOP):

  • WSP 6/12
  • Headers on jacks
  • No 8d@3 as cheaper shear
  • Stairs 3-16d to trimmer
  • Kick plate on basement concrete not a hanger
  • 3-1/2 in stringer remaining
  • 1/2-in drywall under enclosed stairs
